title: The building agent never waits on the developer

options.name: Never wait
options.tradeoff: Claude keeps building; one-way calls are logged and surfaced, and the developer redirects with flags

options.name: Pause on one-way decisions
options.tradeoff: The developer approves risky calls first, but every session stalls until they answer

why: Engagement has to be asynchronous: a turn-based session that blocks on the developer defeats the point of a coding agent.
assumptions: The developer looks at the viewer often enough that flags arrive while they still matter

title: Local state in node:sqlite

options.name: node:sqlite
options.tradeoff: Built into Node 22, no native build; still marked experimental

options.name: better-sqlite3
options.tradeoff: Mature and fast, but a native module that must compile on every machine

options.name: JSON files
options.tradeoff: No dependency, but no transactions between the hooks, MCP server and daemon

why: Hooks, the MCP server and the daemon all write state concurrently, and a plugin must install with no native build step.
assumptions: Node 22 or later everywhere the plugin runs

title: Verify imports with tree-sitter compiled to WASM

options.name: web-tree-sitter (WASM)
options.tradeoff: Fast, portable parsing of Python and TypeScript; imports only, no types

options.name: Language servers
options.tradeoff: Precise resolution, but slow to start and one more process per language

options.name: Regular expressions
options.tradeoff: No dependency, but misses multi-line and aliased imports

why: PostToolUse verification must stay under about 300 ms per edit, and WASM grammars need no native install.
assumptions: Import edges are enough to check a dependency model

title: Background explainer and grader run as headless claude -p

options.name: Headless claude -p from the daemon
options.tradeoff: Uses the developer's own Claude Code and auth; one process per job

options.name: Anthropic API from the daemon
options.tradeoff: Cheaper per call, but needs a separate API key and tool loop

options.name: Subagents in the main session
options.tradeoff: No extra process, but slows the session the developer is building in

why: Keeps explaining and grading off the main session, reuses the developer's setup, and gets structured output with --json-schema.
assumptions: claude is on PATH where the daemon runs

title: The viewer daemon listens on 127.0.0.1 with a token

options.name: Loopback plus token and Host check
options.tradeoff: Safe against other local users and DNS rebinding; the URL carries the token

options.name: Loopback only
options.tradeoff: Simpler, but any local process or web page could read the model

chosen: Loopback plus token and Host check
why: The model and ledger describe private code, and a browser tab on another site must not be able to read them.

title: Grade written answers in two looks

options.name: Model and key first, then the code
options.tradeoff: Cheap when right; a second look reads the code only for partial or wrong answers

options.name: Always read the code
options.tradeoff: Most accurate, but every grade costs a tool-using run

options.name: Key only
options.tradeoff: Cheapest, but marks down answers that are right where the key is incomplete

chosen: Model and key first, then the code
why: Most answers are settled by the model and key; the code is only needed when the developer may know something the key left out.

title: How the model schema moves to v2

options.name: Accept version 1 or 2, always write 2
options.tradeoff: No migration step, since v2 only adds kinds; older plugin builds can't read a model once it has been rewritten

options.name: Stay on version 1 and add optional kinds
options.tradeoff: No version change, but an older build fails on unknown kinds anyway, without a clear version error

options.name: Explicit migrate command
options.tradeoff: Visible upgrade step, but every repo needs a manual run before Claude can write the model

why: v2 is a strict superset of v1 (new node and edge kinds, no changed fields), so a v1 model is already a valid v2 model, and stamping 2 on write gives older builds a clear version error instead of a confusing unknown-kind one.
assumptions: Nobody runs an older Viewport build against a repo after a newer one has rewritten its model

title: How business processes are represented in the model

options.name: Steps as nodes with next edges
options.tradeoff: Branches, traces and implements/covers links work like any other edge; more nodes in the model

options.name: Ordered steps array on the process node
options.tradeoff: Compact and easy to write, but no branches, and edges can't point at a step

chosen: Steps as nodes with next edges
why: Components must implement and tests must cover individual steps, and the proposal's prediction quizzes ask which path runs (\"cancels after shipping\"), which needs branches; edges in this model can only point at nodes.

title: How test and entity links are checked against the code

options.name: Imports and identifier matches
options.tradeoff: Fast and deterministic with the existing tree-sitter scan; a test that reaches code only through another module is not seen

options.name: Run tests with coverage
options.tradeoff: Precise, but slow, language-specific and far over the PostToolUse time budget

options.name: Trust the agent
options.tradeoff: No work, but the proposal's counterweight to the agent misdescribing its work is lost

why: Verification already parses imports for every file under the 300 ms budget (D-003); a covers edge is backed when the test's files import a component that implements the step, and an owns edge when the owner's files name the entity.
assumptions: Tests import the code they cover directly, not only through an entry point in another component

title: Where verification gets its graph lookups for link checks

options.name: Reuse ModelGraph from core.query
options.tradeoff: One index of parents, children and incoming edges; verify now depends on query

options.name: Inline lookups in core.verify
options.tradeoff: Keeps verify independent of query, but duplicates the edge index that query already builds

why: Checking covers edges walks implements, contains and constrained_by edges, and applyReport needs the same test; ModelGraph already indexes exactly that, and core.query has no dependency back on verify, so there is no cycle.

title: How a process view is split into parts

options.name: One part per path, happy path first
options.tradeoff: Each part tells one scenario end to end; steps shared by paths repeat

options.name: Split by element budget
options.tradeoff: Same as the architecture views, but a branch can land mid-part and paths get cut arbitrarily

options.name: Whole process in one view
options.tradeoff: Shows every branch at once; past 7 steps it is a wall of boxes

chosen: One part per path, happy path first
why: The proposal makes scenario the default axis and asks which path runs; next edges with when labels make the paths explicit, and the completeness check already allows shared elements to repeat.
assumptions: The path without when conditions is the happy path

title: Where the phase views live in the viewer

options.name: Phase bar on the Map
options.tradeoff: One place to look; phases are entry views over the same diagram, panel and flags

options.name: A top-level tab per phase
options.tradeoff: Phases are prominent, but six more tabs and duplicate diagram code

why: Every phase view is a query over the one model drawn by the same Diagram, side panel and flag box, so they belong on the Map; the top bar stays Today, Map, Ledger, Ask.

title: How a failure spreads in a what-if

options.name: By dependency mode
options.tradeoff: Sync callers go down, async callers and data dependents degrade; closer to what users see, but trusts the modes in the model

options.name: Everything upstream goes down
options.tradeoff: Simple and never understates, but a queue in between looks as fatal as a direct call

why: The model already records sync, async and data modes, verified against imports for sync and async, and the proposal's question ("Fulfilment goes down. What does the customer see?") hinges on a queue absorbing the outage.
assumptions: A component that calls a failed part asynchronously keeps working, only later

title: Where comparing model revisions gets old revisions

options.name: Local revision snapshots
options.tradeoff: Already kept for 'what changed'; instant and offline, but only the last 200 revisions on this machine

options.name: Git history of model.json
options.tradeoff: Any committed revision on any machine, but only committed ones, and a git call per comparison

why: The daemon already snapshots every revision for the changes list, and readSnapshot gives any of them without shelling out to git inside a request.
